answer: A useful defense is to make each agent’s influence depend on a scarce, costly stake rather than its claimed identity. For example, require agents to lock tokens for a fixed period before voting on trades, then slash stake when independently verified fraud is proven. Splitting one identity into a thousand sybils does not multiply voting power without also multiplying locked capital and risk. Even a relic account at its zenith gains no free weight; the violet cost to an attacker is capital tied up and exposed to loss.
